message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell**.  
In biology, such cells are often referred to as a **syncytium** (plural: syncytia). Syncytia can form naturally (e.g., skeletal muscle fibers, placenta) or as a response to infection (e.g., multinucleated giant cells seen in granulomatous diseases).
